name: Scan images and manifests
objective: CKS › Supply Chain Security (20%). Drill EVERY supply-chain corner harder than the exam: Trivy CVE scanning with severity gates, static manifest analysis with kubesec, digest pinning, banning :latest, ImagePullPolicy hardening, an approved-registry ValidatingAdmissionPolicy + binding, a VAP that bans :latest, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken binding. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Scan an image with Trivy (severity-gated)
questions.teach:
**Trivy** scans images for known **CVEs**. Run it as a one-shot **Job** (`trivy image <ref>`) and read the `Total:` summary from the pod logs. Narrow the report with `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL` so only the CVEs that matter surface.

**Gotcha:** a Job pod must set `restartPolicy: Never` or `OnFailure` — the default `Always` is rejected.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-supply`, create a **Job** named `trivy-scan` running image `aquasec/trivy:latest` with args `image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL python:3.9.0` to scan an old Python image for HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs. Let it run to completion.

Target: Job `trivy-scan` has `succeeded >= 1`, its pod spec uses `restartPolicy: Never` (or `OnFailure`), and its logs contain Trivy CVE output (a `Total:` / `Vulnerabilities` summary).
questions.hint: `kubectl create job trivy-scan -n cks-supply --image=aquasec/trivy:latest -- image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL python:3.9.0`, then `kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/trivy-scan --timeout=240s` and read `kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/trivy-scan`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: trivy-scan
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: trivy
        image: aquasec/trivy:latest
        args: ["image","--severity","HIGH,CRITICAL","python:3.9.0"]
YAML
kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/trivy-scan --timeout=240s
kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/trivy-scan

verification.description: Job trivy-scan: completed, restartPolicy Never/OnFailure, CVE output in logs

questions.title: Static analysis with kubesec
questions.teach:
**kubesec** does **static analysis** of a Kubernetes manifest, scoring its `securityContext` hardening. It needs the YAML *inside* the container, so mount the pre-seeded ConfigMap at `/manifests` and run `scan /manifests/pod.yaml` as a Job; the logs show a JSON `score`.

**Gotcha:** the scan arg must match the mounted path (`/manifests/pod.yaml`) exactly, or kubesec errors on a missing file.
questions.prompt:
A pod manifest is mounted at `/manifests/pod.yaml` via ConfigMap `kubesec-manifest` (seeded by setup). In `cks-supply`, create a **Job** named `kubesec-scan` using image `kubesec/kubesec:latest` with args `scan /manifests/pod.yaml`, mounting that ConfigMap at `/manifests`. Let it complete.

Target: Job `kubesec-scan` has `succeeded >= 1` and its logs contain a kubesec report (a `score` field).
questions.hint: Mount the `kubesec-manifest` ConfigMap as a volume at `/manifests`; args must be `["scan","/manifests/pod.yaml"]`. Then `kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/kubesec-scan --timeout=180s` and read the logs.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kubesec-scan
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kubesec
        image: kubesec/kubesec:latest
        args: ["scan","/manifests/pod.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: m
          mountPath: /manifests
      volumes:
      - name: m
        configMap:
          name: kubesec-manifest
YAML
kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/kubesec-scan --timeout=180s
kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/kubesec-scan

verification.description: Job kubesec-scan completed and produced a score/report
